projects.readmeExcerpt: agent desktop Computer use for AI agents: read and operate desktop apps through the OS accessibility tree. A CLI and C library for macOS, Windows and Linux. A snapshot returns JSON with a ref for every element an agent can act on. The agent acts on a ref and snapshots again to check, with no pixel matching; the loop stays in your agent. Every CLI call runs in its own process. Headless calls still prohibit foreground activation and synthesized input. Snapshots, clipboard reads, screenshots, command output and debug artifacts can contain private desktop content. Keep them out of public logs and uploads. The optional JEV helper sends screen descriptions to a configured model provider; it is separate from the native CLI. See privacy and data handling. projects.name: nanochat
projects.description: The best ChatGPT that $100 can buy.
projects.readmeExcerpt: nanochat nanochat is the simplest experimental harness for training LLMs. It is designed to run on a single GPU node, the code is minimal/hackable, and it covers all major LLM stages including tokenization, pretraining, finetuning, evaluation, and inference. For example, you can train your own GPT 2 capability LLM (which cost $43,000 to train in 2019) for only $48 ( 2 hours of 8XH100 GPU node) and then talk to it over a simple CLI. On a spot instance, the total cost can be closer to $15. More generally, nanochat is configured out of the box to train an entire miniseries of compute optimal models by setting one single complexity dial: depth , the number of layers in the GPT transformer model (GPT 2 capability happens to be approximately depth 26).
